subtopics.title: From Self-Sufficiency to Surplus and Barter

questions.question: Self-sufficiency's brutal constraint was:
options: You consume only what you yourself can make — every skill in every household, nothing done particularly well

questions.question: Surplus is "the hinge of all economic history" because:
options: It releases people from food production — specialists emerge, and specialists must EXCHANGE

questions.question: The double coincidence of wants means:
options: Two people wanting the same good
Wanting twice as much as you have
Trade requires finding someone who has what you want AND wants what you have

questions.question: Barter's four failures are:
options: Double coincidence of wants; indivisibility; no common measure of value; no store of value

subtopics.title: Money and the Evolution of Markets

questions.question: Money's functions are:
options: Medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value — with divisibility making any purchase size work

questions.question: Good commodity moneys — cattle, salt, metals — were chosen for:
options: Durability, divisibility, portability and scarcity — precious metals winning on all four

questions.question: Specialisation and markets "feed each other" because:
options: Specialists need markets to sell in and buy from — and deeper markets support finer specialisation
Both were invented by the state

questions.question: Companies with ownership divided into shares evolved because:
options: Risk could be spread and capital gathered at scales no individual could reach

questions.question: The state's three historic entries into markets were:
options: Involvement in trade, taxation, and financing infrastructure

questions.question: Taxation transformed the ruler's interest because:
options: Larger economies yield larger revenues — rulers acquired a permanent stake in growth, and taxpayers in spending

questions.question: Infrastructure is the classic case for public investment because:
options: It is expensive, benefits everyone, and repays its builder only indirectly — no single trader will build it

questions.question: The analytical thread through all three entries:
options: Each state entry answers a market LIMITATION — term two's intervention logic, seen as history

questions.question: Industrialisation's four components are:
options: Manufacturing, technological progress, mobilisation of energy, mechanisation

questions.question: The mobilisation of energy was "the decisive break" because:
options: Production was unshackled from the limits of living bodies — muscle replaced by water, steam, electricity and oil

questions.question: Industrialisation's costs included:
options: Harsh factory conditions, child labour and pollution — the violations that summoned labour law and regulation

questions.question: South Africa's industrialisation arrived through:
options: MINING — diamonds and gold drawing railways inland and concentrating labour under the migrant system, with social costs still carried

subtopics.title: The Village That Fed Itself — Then Grew Extra

questions.question: Nobody in the self-sufficient village traded because:
options: Nobody had EXTRA — and doing everything meant doing nothing particularly well
Money had not been taxed yet

questions.question: "Extra" changed everything because:
options: One family could eat without every member farming — the clever-handed son becomes the full-time potter

questions.question: Swapping's four miseries were:
options: Slow roads, bad scales, greedy elders, wild animals
The great hunt for the exact partner; the half-goat problem; every deal a fresh argument; wealth that rots or walks off

questions.question: "Money is half a trade, holdable" means:
options: The two halves of a swap were cut apart — sell to anyone, hold the value, buy from anyone else later
Money is worth half its face value
Only half the village used it

questions.question: The tests every good money passes:
options: Sturdy, splittable, scarce, carryable — from cattle and salt to gold, notes and numbers on a phone

questions.question: Strangers trading with strangers required:
options: RULES — honest scales, kept promises, an elder to judge disputes: trust made official

questions.question: Families each owning a SHARE of a big venture meant:
options: No one person carried the whole risk — and capital could gather at new scales

subtopics.title: The Chief, and Then the Machines

questions.question: The chief's three jobs — still the state's today — are:
options: REGULATE the trade, TAX the deals, BUILD what no trader would alone

questions.question: After taxing began, the chief WANTED the market to grow because:
options: His income grew with it — a share of every harvest and deal

questions.question: The machine-day's two new kinds of people were:
options: Those who OWN the machines and those who WORK them — whose arguments become labour relations

questions.question: The village's whole journey, in order:
options: Extra → specialists → money → market (roads, rules, shares) → state → machines
